claude-sonnet-5-5.descriptor: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (released 2026-09-28, https://www.anthropic.com/claude-sonnet-5-5). Default subscription/native-execution Sonnet for CONTRACT-CLEAR execution/review/research, superseding claude-sonnet-5 (Nick, 2026-09-28) — NOT a blanket default: `design_judgment` (architecture/UX-visual-design/hard-judgment/ambiguous-synthesis) and `raw_strength` (hard-algorithmic/debugging/reasoning-heavy) are separate task classes that never resolve here (Nick, 2026-09-28 evening; see the routing_policy chains above). Adaptive thinking; default effort `high` on the raw API but Claude Code itself defaults it to Medium; extended-thinking params (thinking.type:enabled + budget_tokens) NOT accepted — adaptive-only. Sourced from platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/overview (authoritative for id/pricing/limits) + the announcement page for benchmarks: 1M context, 128K output (300K via Batches API with the output-300k-2026-03-24 beta header). $2/$10 per MTok — same headline price as Sonnet 5 — plus cache read $0.20/MTok, cache write $2.50/MTok; Anthropic claims 30%+ faster output and up to 30% lower cost-per-task vs Sonnet 5 via token efficiency. Benchmarks (self-reported announcement page, Sonnet 5.5 / Sonnet 5 / Opus 5.5): Terminal-Bench 4.0 70.6%/10.3%/66.4%; FrontierCode 1.1 (Main, Max effort) 46.2%/42.4%/54.4%; CursorBench 4.0 55.5%/34.1%/57.8%; OSWorld 2.1 (partial) 80.1%/57.0%/81.8%; GDPval-AA v2.1 1844/1449/1846; Chartography (no tools) 61.6%/15.6%/64.4% — beats Sonnet 5 on every listed benchmark and sits close to Opus 5.5 (within a few points on several) at half its per-MTok price. Local Claude Code probe (2026-09-28): `claude -p --model claude-sonnet-5-5 'reply ok'` → stderr `[claude-code:unrecognized_model]` (benign, per the `unrecognized-model-stderr-is-benign` lesson) + stdout `ok`, exit 0 — this harness accepts the id. ICA serves Sonnet 5.5 as of 2026-10-16, re-probed 2026-10-23: completed chat/completions text on bare claude-sonnet-5-5. The older NOT-served note is superseded. Receipt: docs/project_plans/reports/node-sizing-2026-10-23/N10-ica-wire-probe.json.

OpenAI GPT-5.6 Terra via the ICA ccx gateway (free-to-us shared pool) as an agentic Codex lane — same model as gpt-5.6-terra but $0 to the metered budget. ICA can't serve it on the /responses API Codex speaks (Azure api-version-gated), so the router emits `~/ica-codex.sh exec … -m gpt-5.6-terra …`, which auto-starts a local Responses→ChatCompletions shim (agentic_meta_dev/infra/ica-codex-shim/) and drives codex against it. Verified agentic end-to-end (file edits, multi-turn tool loop) 2026-07-29. CAVEAT: reasoning_effort is dropped on tool turns (ICA can't do reasoning+tools on the chat wire) → effort defaults server-side; escalate to metered codex/gpt-5.6-terra or -sol when that matters. NOT genuinely-free (shared_token_pool) so it won't jump free-first chains; enabled + explicit-selectable.

gpt-5.6-luna-ica.descriptor: LEGACY FALLBACK as of 2026-10-16 (still served, 200): ICA gpt-6-luna now replaces this as the ICA free Luna (see the gpt-6-luna entry's ICA row). OpenAI GPT-5.6 Luna via the ICA ccx gateway (free-to-us) as an agentic Codex lane — the cheaper/faster tier. Same routing as gpt-5.6-terra-ica (via `~/ica-codex.sh` + the local Responses shim, agentic_meta_dev/infra/ica-codex-shim/). Verified 2026-07-29; same reasoning_effort-dropped-on-tool-turns caveat. Prefer for lighter review / mechanical edits / cheap second opinions where the free lane is worth the shim overhead. NOT genuinely-free (shared_token_pool); enabled + explicit-selectable.

gpt-5.5.descriptor: OpenAI GPT-5.5 via codex CLI — SUPERSEDED by the gpt-5.6 line (2026-07). Still selectable for compatibility but no longer a default; prefer gpt-5.6-terra (workhorse) / gpt-5.6-sol (hardest) / gpt-5.6-luna (cheap). Reasoning efforts: minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|ultra.

gpt-5.5-pro.descriptor: OpenAI GPT-5.5 Pro via codex CLI — SUPERSEDED by gpt-5.6-sol (2026-07). Retained for compatibility; prefer gpt-5.6-sol for the hardest reasoning.

gemini-3.7-flash.descriptor: Gemini 3.7 Flash — newest Gemini flash tier, found scaffolded-but-unregistered on the ICA `ccx` gateway 2026-08-26 (bare `gemini-3.7-flash`, tool_use + structured output honored, 950,002 prompt tokens measured; not yet in native gemini-cli's known model list, so ICA is currently the ONLY reachable lane — no Google Search grounding there, same as every ICA-proxied Gemini). HEAD-TO-HEAD RUN 2026-08-26 (node_01M0Z7K4QJXD2EWK0BPKD98QVG, n=3 prompts per use case, one operator/session, same ICA ccx /v1/messages transport for both models — see docs/audits/gemini-3.7-vs-3.6-flash-head-to-head-2026-08-26.md in agentic_meta_dev): gemini-3.7-flash matched-or-beat gemini-3.6-flash on every one of 9 prompts (web-research synthesis, second-opinion code/reasoning/SQL critique, SVG icon generation) AND consumed meaningfully fewer output tokens per completion at matched max_tokens budgets — 3.6-flash was truncated mid-answer on 5 of 9 prompts at budgets where 3.7-flash completed cleanly (one SVG prompt needed a 10,000-token budget for 3.6-flash to finish vs 4,471 for 3.7-flash on the same prompt), and 3.6-flash also broke an explicit 'no markdown fences' instruction on one SVG prompt where 3.7-flash complied. RECOMMENDATION: promote to a leg-1/leg-2 ICA-only entry in second_opinion and svg_generation ahead of gemini-3.6-flash's ICA rows, and to web_research's ICA fallback leg (native gemini-3.6-flash stays leg-1 there since it alone has Search grounding) — pending human review of the pilot before flipping enabled/routing_policy. Still NOT auto-routed (n=3 pilot, single session, no adversarial verification of its own scoring).

gpt-5.4-gus.descriptor: GPT-5.4 (`gpt-5.4-gus`) via ICA. Previously recorded as REGRESSED/not-servable on the beta gateway (2026-07-21); on the ccx gateway it is servable again as of 2026-08-26 (200 on both transports, tool_use OK, structured output honored, max completion 128,000). Kept scaffolded/disabled: the upstream gpt-5.4 line retires 2026-08-31 and OpenAI's own migration note points it at gpt-5.6-luna, which is already free on this lane. Documented so a future probe does not re-file it as a discovery.

meta-llama/llama-3-3-70b-instruct.descriptor: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct on the ICA ccx gateway. Pool-cost (not free), and in practice superseded by the FREE meta-llama/llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct-fp8 already on this registry — recorded for completeness, no reason to route here over the free tier.

mistral-medium-2505.descriptor: Mistral Medium 2505 — the first Mistral model on any ICA lane, discovered on the ccx catalog 2026-08-26. Tool use + structured output OK; watsonx-backed, so emits tool-call arguments as a JSON string — call it on /v1/chat/completions, never /v1/messages (the Anthropic-shape translation layer 500s on the string form).

nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super.descriptor: NVIDIA Llama 3.3 Nemotron Super 49B (v1.5 served) on the ICA ccx gateway — discovered and bench-evaluated 2026-10-07 (node_01M4C0PWMG1922F4HQ0TPWZVTG; probe+bench receipt docs/project_plans/reports/model-eval/nemotron-super-2026-10-07/ in agentic_meta_dev). Wire id: bare `nvidia/llama-3.3-nemotron-super` ([1m] suffix 403s). Context window: 131,072 tokens. Economics: FREE (x-litellm-response-cost-original: 0.0). Always-on thinking: the model cannot suppress its chain-of-thought — it always emits reasoning before answering, and on complex tasks the thinking trace leaks into text output (bench T2: leaked ~500-token reasoning trace instead of a clean single-word answer). Tool-use: the model responds to tool declarations but uses a custom <TOOLCALL> XML format, NOT standard Anthropic tool_use blocks or OpenAI function_call/tool_calls — incompatible with AOS infrastructure. Latency: avg ~6s (vs Haiku ~1.8s, GPT-luna ~2.7s) due to always-on thinking. Transport: both /chat/completions (OpenAI-compatible) and /v1/messages (Anthropic-compatible) return 200 on bare id. Bench verdict: correct on extraction/code-fix/summarization/JSON-schema tasks; format failure on classification (T2); registered not routed.
